title: Adaptive safety-band controller with predictive KV prefetch for elastic GPU headroom
creator: Sophie Chen
description: Design and prototype an adaptive safety-band controller that dynamically reserves a minimal GPU memory headroom and drives a predictive KV prefetch policy. Goal is to reduce false-positive evictions during short bursts and improve throughput for continuous-batching workloads without increasing tail latency or risking OOMs.
background: We currently use static headroom heuristics that either over-reserve (wasting GPU capacity) or under-reserve (causing KV/activation evictions and OOM cascades under bursty traffic). Continuous batching and KV cache growth patterns vary by tenant and model sequence-length distribution, so static policies are suboptimal. Prior tickets explored slab allocation and probabilistic headroom; this work focuses on a lightweight controller that combines short-horizon forecasting with a small, elastic prefetch budget for hot KV slots.
proposal_summary: Implement a low-latency safety-band controller that maintains a soft reserve (safety band) sized by a predictive model (10s window) that uses token-rate, active-seq-length quantiles, and kv-hit-rate. Complement this with a predictive KV prefetcher that preloads the top-N hot KV shards into an ephemeral prefetch tier when forecasted demand exceeds threshold. The controller exposes tunables for: min_safety_mb, max_safety_ratio, prefetch_budget_mb, and prefetch_eviction_policy.
design_details: Telemetry inputs: per-request sequence length, token emission rate, KV miss/hit latency, per-tenant KV cardinality histogram sampled at 1s

Controller loop: every 2s compute expected transient memory delta for next 10s using EWMA and short autoregressive predictor; set safety-band = clamp(predicted_delta * safety_multiplier, min_safety_mb, max_safety_ratio * gpu_free_mem)

Prefetcher: rank hot KV keys by recent access frequency and predicted upcoming accesses; prefetch into ephemeral prefetch pool up to prefetch_budget_mb; mark prefetched slots with lower eviction priority than regular cache until pool pressure rises
Interactions with scheduler: scheduler treats safety-band as soft reservation; when offered batch would violate safety-band, controller signals batch-split or fallback to a lighter model variant
Fallbacks: on sustained forecast error, escalate safety-band to a conservative cap and surface incident in telemetry channel
acceptance_criteria: End-to-end prototype deployed in canary pool without OOM incidents for 72h under synthetic bursty workload
Prefetcher reduces average KV miss latency by >= 20% on workload with 5-20% temporal locality
Net GPU utilization increases by >= 6% over baseline static-headroom config while tail latency (95th token latency) does not regress >5%
Controller exposes metrics and knobs in Console and has a default policy usable without per-tenant tuning
tasks: Implement controller loop and lightweight predictor (2s cadence)
Implement prefetch pool and ranking pipeline in runtime (C++/CUDA) with feature flag
Add token-level telemetry hooks and a compact reservoir sampler for KV cardinality
Integration tests with batcher to simulate batch-split fallback path
Create bench harness and synthetic workloads (varied seq-lengths, hot-key locality)
Run canary on 3 nodes then expand to 10 nodes; collect metrics and iterate
Document API knobs and default policy in internal design doc and Console feature page
Open PRs: runtime changes, telemetry schema, console metric wiring
benchmarks_and_results: Local sim (single-GPU) with synthetic traces: safety-band + prefetch reduced eviction count by 78% and saved 4.9% average token cost
Canary perf run (initial): 48-hour run showed 4% uplift in useful GPU time and 12% KV miss latency improvement for medium locality traces
Regression note: one workload with extreme long tails (>10k tokens) saw 7% increase in 95th latency; controller adjusted safety_multiplier upward in next run
rollout_plan: Feature-flagged prototype to canary pool (3 nodes) - Week 1
Observe 48-72h; tune default safety_multiplier and prefetch_budget - Week 2
Expand to 10-node canary, include a mix of tenant silhouettes - Week 3
Gradual ramp to 30% of serving fleet behind a rollout policy with automatic rollback on OOMs or latency regressions - Week 4
Full rollout contingent on meeting acceptance criteria and runbook approval
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: predictive model underestimates burst leading to OOM. Mitigation: hard OOM guard plus conservative upper clamp and immediate rollback signal; circuit-breaker in control loop

Risk: prefetch pool competes with weights and activations in memory. Mitigation: prefetch_budget_mb bounded and prefetch eviction priority lower than active KV hits; controller reduces prefetch_budget under memory pressure
Risk: metric noise causes oscillation of safety-band. Mitigation: add hysteresis and minimum hold time for adjustments, use EWMA smoothing
decisions: Decision: use a 10s prediction horizon for safety-band sizing to balance responsiveness vs noise
Decision: prefetch pool implemented as ephemeral tier with lower eviction priority rather than permanently increasing KV allocations
Decision: expose only three Console knobs initially (safety_multiplier, min_safety_mb, prefetch_budget_mb) to avoid operator complexity
open_questions: How to incorporate multi-tenant weight-sharing scenarios where model weights may be partially offloaded?
Should prefetch ranking include model-aware heuristics (attention map hot-spots) beyond simple access frequency?
Are existing telemetry retention policies sufficient for training the predictor without incurring high storage costs?
